companies.name: Temporal
companies.summary: Preserves workflow state so multi-step agents can resume after service failures and wait for human decisions.
companies.proposedUse: Run a document-review workflow that survives outages and resumes after a supervisor approves the next step.
capabilities: Persistent workflow history and recoverable execution
Retries around external services and model calls
Human approvals inside long-running workflows
companies.limitation: Durable execution preserves progress; it does not make a mistaken model decision correct.

companies.name: E2B
companies.summary: Provides an isolated machine for an agent to execute code, work with files and use software.
companies.proposedUse: Let a supervised analysis agent process approved spreadsheets in a disposable environment.
capabilities: Per-session microVMs with shell, files and browser
Snapshots and sandbox lifecycle APIs
Network policy and deployment in supported customer clouds
companies.limitation: Review outbound network rules, secrets, retention and the actual isolation boundary before connecting sensitive systems.

companies.name: Daytona
companies.summary: Creates programmable execution environments for AI-generated code and parallel agent tasks.
companies.proposedUse: Run coding and data-cleaning experiments with disposable workspaces and explicit resource budgets.
capabilities: Create and remove sandboxes through SDKs
Execute code with streamed output
Run parallel, stateful agent environments
companies.limitation: Isolation and fast startup do not validate the code or authorize external actions.

companies.name: LlamaIndex
companies.summary: Extracts document text, tables and fields with page locations; offers both hosted parsing and a lightweight local CPU pipeline.
companies.proposedUse: Parse supervision reports with clickable evidence and benchmark a local first pass before sending difficult pages to a larger model.
companies.availability: Commercial platform; local parser and separately licensed model weights
capabilities: LlamaParse extracts structured document content
Bounding boxes link output to source regions
OCRia-nano-1 runs locally through LiteParse
companies.limitation: Nano has no chart-to-table model; complex tables, handwriting and degraded scans need separate evaluation.

companies.name: Nango
companies.summary: Connects agents to business APIs with authentication, synchronization, tool execution and action logs.
companies.proposedUse: Connect a sandbox intake agent to an approved ticketing API and verify every requested write.
capabilities: Managed API authorization and token lifecycle
Tools, event triggers and data synchronization
Scoped permissions and action audit trails
companies.limitation: A supported connector does not establish institutional permission to read or modify a system.

companies.name: Qodo
companies.summary: Reviews code changes against repository context and team rules, with new session-level review across an agent’s pull requests.
companies.proposedUse: Compare reviewer effort and defects on agent-written prototype changes against the current review process.
companies.availability: Commercial platform; selected features beta or research preview
capabilities: Context-aware pull-request review and cross-repository checks
Team rules and guarded approval workflows
Agent Session Review assembles decisions and related PRs
companies.limitation: Session review is a research preview and auto-approval is beta; measure missed defects and retain required reviewers.

companies.name: Harness Cosmos
companies.summary: Coordinates engineering work from tickets through code, tests and review using technology acquired from Augment Code.
companies.proposedUse: Test a ticket-to-reviewed-PR workflow for a bounded internal maintenance backlog.
companies.note: Harness announced the acquisition of selected Augment Code assets, including Cosmos, the Auggie CLI and Code Context Engine, on 8 October 2026.
companies.evidenceNote: Harness announced the acquisition of selected Augment Code assets, including Cosmos, the Auggie CLI and Code Context Engine, on 8 October 2026.
capabilities: Events and schedules trigger engineering workflows
Specialized agents plan, review and verify changes
Code context informs follow-up work after failed checks
companies.limitation: Integration, code access and merge policy remain organization-specific; the selected assets now sit with Harness.

companies.name: Cursor
companies.summary: Combines desktop and command-line development with cloud agents that implement and test changes in separate environments.
companies.proposedUse: Compare agent-assisted prototype work with existing IDE tools using accepted changes and review time.
capabilities: Codebase context and interactive development
Parallel cloud agents with their own environments
Reviewable code changes and demonstrations
companies.limitation: Generated code still needs repository-specific tests, security review and controlled release access.

companies.name: CodeRabbit
companies.summary: Reviews pull requests and helps teams prioritize, understand, secure and verify agent-generated changes.
companies.proposedUse: Add independent review to an internal pilot repository and track actionable findings per reviewer minute.
capabilities: Automated PR review with concrete suggestions
Change prioritization and codebase risk visibility
Verification workflows alongside code review
companies.limitation: Automated review can miss business intent or create noisy findings; evaluate against a labelled defect set.

companies.name: Tessl
companies.summary: Provides a shared registry for agent skills and context, with evaluations and checks as those instructions change.
companies.proposedUse: Create a tested registry of engineering skills and compare agent task success before promoting a new version.
capabilities: Searchable organization and private skill registries
Before-and-after evaluation of context changes
Policy checks and reusable review workflows
companies.limitation: A shared skill can spread errors as well as good practice; keep ownership and regression evidence per version.

companies.name: Patronus AI
companies.summary: Studies agent failures and develops task environments, trace benchmarks and training data for better behavior.
companies.proposedUse: Use trace-level failure categories when constructing an evaluation set for a supervised knowledge agent.
companies.availability: Research outputs and commercial research engagement
companies.note: Current positioning is a behavioral research lab; avoid describing the company only as an evaluation dashboard.
companies.evidenceNote: Current positioning is a behavioral research lab; avoid describing the company only as an evaluation dashboard.
capabilities: Environment-based assessment of agent judgment
TRAIL benchmark for locating failures in traces
Research and data across coding and knowledge tasks
companies.limitation: Research benchmarks are not a turnkey guarantee of reliability on institutional workflows.

companies.name: HiddenLayer
companies.summary: Inventories AI assets, inspects model supply chains, simulates attacks and monitors runtime threats.
companies.proposedUse: Test an AI application against an agreed attack set and connect findings to existing security response.
capabilities: AI application and model discovery
Model supply-chain analysis and attack simulation
Runtime monitoring with security-tool integrations
companies.limitation: Detection coverage and false-positive rates depend on model, application and deployment integration.

companies.name: WitnessAI
companies.summary: Provides visibility and policies for employee AI use, applications and supported agent tool activity.
companies.proposedUse: Compare policy enforcement on legitimate and disallowed tool calls in a controlled workflow.
capabilities: Observe employee and agent AI activity
Control supported tool access and sensitive data flows
Runtime defense and policy-based governance
companies.limitation: Only traffic and action paths that reach the deployed controls can be governed.

companies.name: Modal
companies.summary: Runs model inference, training jobs and agent sandboxes on programmable cloud infrastructure.
companies.proposedUse: Benchmark a permitted open-model workload by cost per accepted result and sustained throughput.
capabilities: Autoscaling dedicated inference and model APIs
GPU training and fine-tuning jobs
Isolated environments for agent execution
companies.limitation: Provider regions, workload costs and network boundaries must fit the institution’s deployment requirements.

companies.name: Baseten
companies.summary: Combines dedicated model serving, training, execution sandboxes and controls over model access.
companies.proposedUse: Evaluate a narrow document classifier or extraction model against a general-model baseline.
capabilities: Dedicated inference for specialized models
Custom training through code and SDKs
Model-access, routing and usage controls
companies.limitation: Specialization only helps when task quality, latency and total operating cost improve on a representative workload.

companies.name: Fireworks AI
companies.summary: Runs, routes and trains open models so organizations can tailor model systems to particular tasks.
companies.proposedUse: Compare routing among open models on an expert-reviewed retrieval or classification workload.
capabilities: Hosted inference for open and custom models
Model ensembling and per-task routing
Training to adapt models to domain workloads
companies.limitation: Provider claims about speed or savings need workload-specific validation and appropriate data residency.

companies.name: Flower Labs
companies.summary: Supports collaborative model training and evaluation across organizations while keeping training data distributed.
companies.proposedUse: Test a jointly trained model with synthetic partner datasets before considering restricted institutional data.
capabilities: Federated training and evaluation with common ML frameworks
Secure aggregation and differential-privacy options
Deployment across separate institutional environments
companies.limitation: Federation alone does not guarantee privacy; updates, consent and re-identification risks still need controls.

companies.name: Zama
companies.summary: Uses fully homomorphic encryption to support confidential transactions and assets on public blockchains.
companies.proposedUse: Study disclosure, auditability and performance trade-offs in a financial-infrastructure research sandbox.
capabilities: Computation on encrypted transaction information
Confidential transfers and tokenized assets
Programmable disclosure and compliance features
companies.limitation: Cryptographic confidentiality does not establish legal suitability, economic value or unrestricted production performance.

companies.name: PQShield
companies.summary: Builds software and hardware cryptography for migration to standardized quantum-resistant security.
companies.proposedUse: Assess crypto-agility and pilot hybrid key exchange on a non-production service.
capabilities: Software libraries for post-quantum and hybrid algorithms
Integration with authentication and secure communication
Hardware and embedded cryptographic implementations
companies.limitation: Migration requires compatibility testing, dependency inventory and validation of the exact implementation.

companies.name: Viam
companies.summary: Connects robotics hardware to software, data capture, remote operations and controlled fleet updates.
companies.proposedUse: Explore sensor and inspection data collection for an infrastructure pilot with explicit operating limits.
capabilities: Common APIs across sensors and robotic components
On-device controls and declared movement limits
Remote diagnostics and staged fleet rollouts
companies.limitation: Safety claims depend on hardware, environment and configured limits; a platform is not task certification.

companies.name: FieldAI
companies.summary: Develops robot autonomy for unstructured construction, industrial and infrastructure environments.
companies.proposedUse: Assess repeatable site-inspection missions and the quality of evidence they provide to project supervision.
capabilities: Robot navigation across changing physical environments
Risk-aware models combining learned and physical information
Deployment across supported robot forms and industrial sites
companies.limitation: Site access, safety, hardware and task-level performance require local validation; avoid universal autonomy claims.

companies.name: Arcade
companies.summary: Enforces user-scoped authorization and runtime policies as agents call business tools, including pre-authorization for planned multi-service work.
companies.proposedUse: Test user-scoped authorization and explicit write permissions for workflow agents.
capabilities: User-delegated authorization for connected tools
Per-action policies and audit records
Bundled pre-authorization before multi-service tasks
companies.limitation: Approval to connect a service is separate from approval for each consequential action; validate the actual action scope.

companies.name: Zep
companies.summary: Builds temporal context graphs so agents can retrieve relationships and distinguish current facts from superseded information.
companies.proposedUse: Test whether project assistants correctly distinguish current decisions from superseded information.
capabilities: Temporal graphs retain when facts become valid or obsolete
Hybrid retrieval combines graph, vector and text search
Graphiti supports pluggable graph and model backends
companies.limitation: Entity resolution, permissions and deletion must be tested; retaining a fact’s history does not prove it is true.

companies.name: Letta
companies.summary: Builds persistent agents whose memory and context can continue across conversations, tools and working sessions.
companies.proposedUse: Prototype a long-running project assistant with inspectable memory and explicit retention rules.
capabilities: Persistent agent identity and memory across sessions
Concurrent conversations sharing agent memory
Inspectable context and memory workflows
companies.limitation: Shared memory needs ownership, isolation, retention and correction rules before it handles institutional material.

trends.title: Execution environments for long-running agents
trends.summary: Durable workflows preserve progress; isolated machines give agents controlled places to execute code.
trends.whyNow: Temporal, E2B and Daytona expose execution infrastructure separately from the model, making recovery and containment explicit design choices.
trends.application: Run a supervised workflow with recoverable state, disposable code execution and a clear approval boundary.
trends.experiment: Interrupt a 20-step sandbox workflow, restart it and inspect which actions resume, repeat or remain blocked.
trends.measure: Recovery success, duplicate side effects, resource cost and containment of denied network activity.

applicationsByLens.its: Run a supervised workflow with recoverable state, disposable code execution and a clear approval boundary.
applicationsByLens.frontier: Run a supervised workflow with recoverable state, disposable code execution and a clear approval boundary.

trends.title: Model infrastructure for specific workloads
trends.summary: Model serving, adaptation and routing are becoming a separate layer of enterprise AI design.
trends.whyNow: Baseten, Modal and Fireworks combine serving and adaptation with infrastructure controls; the useful comparison is performance on a real workload.
trends.application: Evaluate a small set of model and serving combinations for one measurable institutional task.
trends.experiment: Run a fixed, expert-reviewed dataset across general and specialized models with identical acceptance criteria.
trends.measure: Cost per accepted result, tail latency, throughput, quality and deployment constraints.

applicationsByLens.its: Evaluate a small set of model and serving combinations for one measurable institutional task.
applicationsByLens.frontier: Evaluate a small set of model and serving combinations for one measurable institutional task.

trends.title: Learning and computing across data boundaries
trends.summary: Federated learning and encrypted computation offer different ways to collaborate without routinely centralizing raw data.
trends.whyNow: Flower provides distributed learning infrastructure; Zama demonstrates encrypted execution in financial applications. Their privacy guarantees and costs differ.
trends.application: Explore multi-institution analysis using synthetic data and an explicit threat model before considering restricted information.
trends.experiment: Compare a centralized baseline with a federated or encrypted design on one narrowly defined task.
trends.measure: Utility loss, computation cost, leakage tests, operational complexity and participant control.
watchouts: Federation is not privacy by itself

applicationsByLens.its: Explore multi-institution analysis using synthetic data and an explicit threat model before considering restricted information.
applicationsByLens.wbg: Explore multi-institution analysis using synthetic data and an explicit threat model before considering restricted information.
applicationsByLens.frontier: Explore multi-institution analysis using synthetic data and an explicit threat model before considering restricted information.

trends.title: Migration to quantum-resistant cryptography
trends.summary: Organizations can assess cryptographic dependencies and test standardized post-quantum and hybrid implementations now.
trends.whyNow: NIST finalized its first three standards in 2024; vendors including PQShield provide implementation paths, making migration distinct from waiting for useful quantum computers.
trends.application: Prioritize long-lived sensitive information and assess where cryptographic dependencies can be changed safely.
trends.experiment: Pilot a compatible hybrid key-exchange implementation on a non-production service.
trends.measure: Interoperability, latency, key and certificate handling, rollback and inventory coverage.

applicationsByLens.its: Prioritize long-lived sensitive information and assess where cryptographic dependencies can be changed safely.
applicationsByLens.frontier: Prioritize long-lived sensitive information and assess where cryptographic dependencies can be changed safely.

trends.title: Software agents across the development cycle
trends.summary: AI systems that plan, edit, test and maintain software using the same development tools as engineers.
trends.whyNow: The scope now includes event-triggered engineering, review and verification. Qodo introduced session-level review on 18 November 2026; Harness acquired selected Augment assets to connect coding with delivery.
trends.application: Use a supervised agent to repair a sandbox application, generate tests or modernize a small internal service; engineers retain review and release authority.
trends.experiment: Compare an agent-assisted team with the existing process on 10 small repository tasks, using the same acceptance criteria and code review.
trends.measure: Accepted task completion, reviewer time, introduced defects, elapsed time and cost per accepted change.
watchouts: Reviewing business intent across multiple changes
Quality and cost per accepted change

applicationsByLens.its: Test a software agent on a real maintenance backlog within existing source-control, identity, test and review controls.
applicationsByLens.frontier: Examine how longer-running software agents change the economics of building and maintaining products, and where review becomes the limiting factor.

trends.title: Context graphs and persistent agent memory
trends.summary: Systems that preserve relevant facts, relationships and prior decisions across tasks, sometimes recording when a fact was true and where it came from.
trends.whyNow: Temporal context graphs and shared memory across concurrent conversations make longer-lived assistants practical to test. The key question is whether they retain the right facts and retire obsolete ones.
trends.application: Create a project assistant that distinguishes an approved current decision from a superseded draft and cites the underlying document.
trends.experiment: Build a small, permissioned project corpus with deliberately conflicting dated records; compare standard retrieval with temporal or structured memory.
trends.measure: Correct handling of superseded facts, source accuracy, deletion behavior, access-control fidelity and retrieval cost.

trends.title: Interoperable agents and permissioned tools
trends.summary: Common interfaces through which agents find tools, access systems and delegate tasks while preserving identity and authorization.
trends.whyNow: Tool connectivity is being paired with identity, permission scopes and runtime controls. Arcade’s September 2026 release gathers planned tool authorizations before a long task starts.
trends.application: Connect a portfolio-research assistant to approved document search and a calculation service, with separate permissions and an auditable record for every tool call.
trends.experiment: Connect two approved read-only systems and one specialist agent; verify identity propagation, denied actions, cancellation and complete audit records.
trends.measure: Integration effort, successful task handoffs, unauthorized-action rejection and diagnosability of failures.

applicationsByLens.its: Connect approved search, analytics and specialist tools without giving an agent broad credentials or rebuilding each integration.
applicationsByLens.frontier: Follow whether common protocols produce interchangeable tools and agents across vendors while preserving identity, cancellation and clear accountability.

trends.title: Evaluation and observability for agent behavior
trends.summary: Tools that record an agent's actions and test whether complete tasks meet defined standards for quality, safety and cost.
trends.whyNow: Assessment increasingly covers whole work traces, related code changes and tool use. New session-review products complement established trace benchmarks and application attack testing.
trends.application: Evaluate a complaints-supervision assistant for evidence fidelity, multilingual quality, correct tool use and proper escalation before deployment.
trends.experiment: Create 50 expert-reviewed cases, including ambiguous and adversarial examples, and compare two candidate systems using identical rubrics.
trends.measure: End-to-end success, false confidence, permission violations, latency, cost and agreement between automated scores and expert review.
watchouts: Regression coverage after tool or model changes

trends.title: Document intelligence that preserves usable evidence
trends.summary: Turn scans, tables, forms and long reports into structured records that preserve their location and meaning in the original document.
trends.whyNow: LlamaIndex released OCRia-1.5 on 18 November 2026 and a local CPU parser on 23 November. This supports testing a fast first pass plus stronger processing for difficult pages.
trends.application: Make project reports and supporting annexes easier to search and compare without detaching a figure, date or statement from its original table, page and document version.

applicationsByLens.its: Improve the document pipeline feeding institutional search and agents, including difficult PDFs and tables, with traceable extraction and retained source permissions.
applicationsByLens.wbg: Compare indicators across public project reports and annexes while retaining page-level evidence and flagging changes in definitions, reporting periods and units.

trends.experiment: Use 50 public reports with scanned pages, multilingual text and complex tables. Build a human-checked reference set of fields and supporting page regions, then compare two extraction approaches on the same files.
trends.measure: Correct fields with correct units and periods; preserved table relationships; unsupported values; usable source locations; reviewer time and cost per accepted record.

trends.title: General-purpose robot policies
trends.summary: AI models that translate perception and instructions into robot actions, aiming to transfer skills across tasks or hardware.
trends.whyNow: Autonomy is moving from model demonstrations into selected physical-site deployments. FieldAI announced a Kajima construction deployment in November 2026; Viam provides hardware integration and fleet-operation infrastructure.
trends.application: Explore future applications in infrastructure inspection, repetitive handling and worker safety, including how costs and labor impacts differ in developing economies.
trends.experiment: With a robotics partner, specify one constrained inspection or handling task and benchmark against an established specialized solution.
trends.measure: Successful cycles without intervention, safety incidents, recovery time, total operating cost and performance in unfamiliar conditions.

signals.title: A local first pass for document processing
signals.text: LlamaIndex released OCRia-nano-1 for local CPU parsing through LiteParse. Complex charts and degraded scans still require separate handling.

signals.title: Reviewing the coding agent’s complete session
signals.text: Qodo introduced Agent Session Review as a research preview, connecting related pull requests, agent decisions and evidence for a human review.

signals.title: Document extraction keeps source locations
signals.text: OCRia-1.5 adds improved document structure and bounding-box placement in LlamaParse; evaluation should include whether readers can verify each extracted field.

signals.title: Construction autonomy enters selected deployments
signals.text: FieldAI published a Kajima construction deployment announcement. Site-level capability and safety should be checked before extrapolating to other infrastructure projects.

signals.title: Augment technology joins the Harness portfolio
signals.text: Harness acquired selected Augment Code assets including Cosmos, Auggie CLI and the Code Context Engine. The radar identifies Cosmos as an ecosystem product.

signals.title: Authorize planned tool access before a long task
signals.text: Arcade added bundled pre-authorization for planned tool calls while retaining user-scoped authorization and per-action enforcement.

notes: 21 new company/product records and 3 expanded existing records; 4 new trends and 6 updated existing trends. All listed sources were read on 24 November 2026.

Do not label every included entity a startup. Harness Cosmos is an ecosystem product based on selected acquired Augment assets; Flower and several infrastructure companies include open-source projects; Patronus currently describes itself as a research lab.
Evidence dates are publication dates only when explicitly visible. Null evidenceDate means the current product page is undated, not a new launch on the verification date.
Proposed WBG and ITS uses are analyst suggestions. None of these source checks establish WBG adoption, procurement approval or technical suitability.
The Kajima customer PDF returned 403. The FieldAI announcement title/date and current company product page were read; no detailed customer deployment metrics are asserted.
When merging, rebuild bidirectional trend/company links from company.trendIds. LlamaIndex also links to the existing on-device-ai trend; FieldAI also links to project-supervision.
Coverage is expanded but is not an exhaustive census, and inherited records not included in this refresh must keep their older checked dates.

Best new spotlights: LlamaIndex (documents with source evidence and local processing), Temporal/E2B (recoverable workflows and isolated execution), Qodo (review of complete coding sessions), FieldAI (physical-site evidence). Each should use exact same company record in radar and video.
